clue.text: Extra small sleepwear for Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was the Oxford don famous for swapping the opening sounds within his words

parts.note: the sleepwear is a nightie, said as two syllables; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A shopper asks for the smallest size of nightwear, oddly on behalf of a dead clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGH-TEE with its N and T swapped becomes TIE-NEE, which is spelt TINY. Tiny Tim starts the Christmas Carol theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is a plain synonym for very small, the sense of a clothing size labelled extra small.

clue.text: Old men host TV show

parts.note: fathers, the older generation of men
a host is a great multitude, especially of soldiers

explanation.surface: Elderly gentlemen present a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic BBC sitcom about the Home Guard in the Second World War, a force largely of older men, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad's Army is the title of a long-running British television comedy series.

clue.text: Bond eating his superior porridge

indicators.note: something eating takes another thing inside it, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a bond or tie is something that links
M is James Bond's boss in the spy novels and films

explanation.surface: James Bond tucks into his boss's breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' and 'his superior' set up the spy, but Bond is just a tie. Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, as in the sitcom Porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing porridge means serving time in prison, so porridge is slang for a jail term.

clue.text: Mike brewed Beamish in former wife's address

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: brewing mixes and stews ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; Beamish is an Irish stout

explanation.surface: A man called Mike brews stout for his ex-wife's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a house but is a form of address. Memsahib was how a married European woman was addressed in colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: Memsahib was the respectful title used for a married white woman in the Raj, a term now historical.

clue.text: Northern European screen princess

parts.note: to screen is to scan or check
Diana, Princess of Wales, was known as Di

explanation.surface: A Nordic princess appears on the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandi is informal for Scandinavian, a person or thing from the countries of northern Europe.

clue.text: Spitting Image covering heavy metal band's number one

indicators.note: a covering goes around something, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a dead ringer is someone's spitting image
lead is a famously heavy metal

explanation.surface: The satirical puppet show Spitting Image covers a heavy-metal band's chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal band' reads as one music phrase, but heavy metal is the element and the band belongs to the definition. Spitting Image was a British TV puppet satire.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the person heading a gang, so the chief of a band of rogues.

clue.text: Actor's nameless brother

indicators.note: nameless means lacking a name, so the abbreviation for name is dropped

parts.note: a Jacobin was a Dominican friar in France, a religious brother

explanation.surface: An actor talks about his brother who has no name.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop N, the abbreviation for name. Sir Derek Jacobi is a celebrated English stage and screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Derek Jacobi is a famous actor, so the answer is an example of the category given.

clue.text: Half of 2 and 3 done

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that follows half when telling the time at 2:30 or 3:30
second meaning: over, finished, gone by

explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to 2 and 3, but they are hours on a clock: half ___ two, half ___ three. The Ghost of Christmas Past fits the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done is over and finished, belonging to time gone by, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: Slice of tiramisu knocked back in China

explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain, so its capital letter misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a style of Japanese porcelain, and china is the general word for porcelain ware.

clue.text: Ah, Daniel Craig's heading off for meal in Leon

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the first letter of the name is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Daniel Craig sets off to eat in the Mexican city of León.
explanation.walkthrough: León is a city in Mexico, so a meal there is a Mexican dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a rolled tortilla with a filling, a typical Mexican dish such as one eats in that country.

clue.text: Sycophant is curious about travel agents retiring

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the whole is read in the opposite direction
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: nosey means inquisitive
reps are holiday company representatives at resorts

explanation.definitionFit: A yes-person agrees with everything their superior says, the behaviour of a fawning flatterer.

clue.text: Spirit of game broken by Hearts wingers in shoot-out

indicators.note: something broken by another thing is split open with that thing in the gap

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

parts.note: the first and last letters of the hyphenated word

clue.text: Mark King with a temperature in school

indicators.note: in places the group of pieces inside another word

parts.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school
CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark King' reads as a person's name, but Mark is the definition. The answer also gives Bob Cratchit, with 18 Across, for the theme.

clue.text: Latitude involved in rise of The Sun

parts.note: to soar is to rise high
L is the abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: A newspaper story on the rising freedom of The Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'The Sun' suggests the tabloid; it is the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar is the adjective meaning relating to the sun, so it swaps for the phrase.

clue.text: Gossip from account clerk

parts.note: a tale is a story or account
a teller is a bank clerk

explanation.surface: Office rumours come from a clerk in accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale-teller spreads stories about others, so the word names a gossip or telltale.

clue.text: List of title's prime locations — almost 25

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
prime locations are the prime-numbered positions in a word: second, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: the letters in positions two, three and five
the answer to 25 Across is the archetypal miser

explanation.walkthrough: The 25 is Scrooge, whose name means a miser; dropping its last letter leaves MISE.

clue.text: Stir up memories of uplifting Janáček overture

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
here the word is used for its letters, which contain part of the answer, not as an opening piece

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the name and start of the next word

explanation.surface: An inspiring overture by the Czech composer Janáček brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overture' looks like a selector for the first letter, but the answer sits across both words.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke something is to call it to mind, bringing memories of it back.

clue.text: True blue perhaps changing direction at first

indicators.note: changing direction swaps one side for the other, right for left, at the start of the word

parts.note: royal blue is a shade of blue

explanation.surface: A true-blue loyalist is perhaps changing direction.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the front becomes L (left). True blue is an idiom for staunchly loyal, which hides the definition in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: True means faithful, the same as a loyal friend who stays steadfast.

clue.text: Singer cut Ma Baker's last line

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut
taken as written

parts.note: the final letter of the name
a ley line is an alignment of ancient sites

explanation.walkthrough: Ma Baker was a Boney M song. Bob Marley was the reggae singer; Bob Cratchit and Marley are both in the Christmas Carol theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley was a Jamaican reggae singer, so he is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Top horse to dominate

parts.note: to top something is to best it
to horse is an old verb meaning to ride, or a ride is a mount

explanation.surface: The leading racehorse will dominate the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to tower over or rule something, as a colossus stands astride it.

clue.text: Dance round and round

parts.note: a disc is a round shape
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Dancing in circles, round and round the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club for dancing to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Porn star introducing Wild At Heart in a threatening manner

indicators.note: introducing brings something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Stormy Daniels is an American porn star

indicators.note: at heart means at the core, so the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters

explanation.surface: A porn star appears in the David Lynch film Wild at Heart, playing a menacing part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild At Heart' looks like a single film title, but it splits into the word and its selector.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormily means in a turbulent, angry way, like an approaching storm, so with menace.

clue.text: Engineers union in another meeting

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a match is a marriage or union

explanation.surface: Engineers' trade union holding another meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents, a further sporting encounter.

clue.text: See 18
Supply teacher for the most part a goddess

indicators.note: most of the word but not all, so the final letter goes
supply as an adjective means pliant and bendy, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply teacher' reads as a stand-in teacher, but supply (supple) is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, crossroads and the night.

clue.text: Dickensian character goes mad about return of monster

about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: taken as written
an orc is a monster of fantasy fiction

explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge is the miser at the heart of Dickens's A Christmas Carol, the theme.

parts.note: the final letter

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is a Christian festival, and a feast is a religious festival or celebration.

clue.text: America's revolutionary baloney sandwiches

parts.note: the United States
